footnotes: Tesla reports segment gross profit, not segment operating income; the automotive segment includes services and other.

Net income is attributable to common stockholders, after $60M to noncontrolling interests. Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Cash & investments = cash, equivalents and short-term investments.
Diluted EPS by quarter as reported in the 10-Qs; fourth quarters are calculated (net income ÷ estimated diluted shares) because EPS does not add across quarters.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Tesla's revenue fell 2.9% to $94.8B in 2025 as automotive revenue dropped 9.8% to $69.5B. Energy generation and storage grew 26.6% to $12.8B and services and other 19.0% to $12.5B. Operating income fell 38.5% to $4.4B as R&D spending rose 41%.
Net income fell 46.5% to $3.8B, or $1.08 per diluted share. Free cash flow rose 73.7% to $6.2B because capital spending fell, and cash and investments reached $44.1B.
highlights: Energy segment gross profit rose 44.0% to $3.8B, a 29.8% margin.
Energy storage deployments reached a record 46.7 GWh, up 49%.
Gross margin edged up to 18.0% from 17.9% despite lower vehicle sales.
Free cash flow rose to $6.2B, and net cash reached $35.7B.
watch: Automotive revenue fell for a second year, and Q4 deliveries were down 16%.
Operating margin dropped to 4.6% from 7.2% as R&D rose 41% to $6.4B.
